appendText.text: REV 26 (SEC-24 M-26, m-87): the arming decision is the CLOSED, TOTAL pure function decide(perRealm, requiredIds) of rev 26 section B.5. requiredIds MUST equal the canonical required-realm set exactly - the required F-rows of table W6-T, ids F1..F21 - with no missing id, no duplicate, no extra and no unknown id; perRealm must be an array in which every required id appears exactly once. A realm demonstrates absence ONLY when all required fields affirmatively validate (measurable===true, no error, timedOut===false, typeof==='undefined', descriptor===undefined, the pre-captured native reference value exactly undefined, constructed===false, repetitions consistent). null, 'object', a missing or undefined field, an exception, a timeout, disagreement or any other value yields shared_worker_block_unverified. Deterministic precedence: malformed, incomplete or unverified evidence => shared_worker_block_unverified exit 18 FIRST; otherwise any measured presence => shared_worker_present exit 18; only complete, valid, unanimous measured absence arms. REV 26 (OWNER-24, OWNER-25): arming additionally requires that the probe ran in the SAME browser process, executable, arguments, environment and context configuration the run will use, and that the browser passed the complete W6-T conformance gate; the supported-browser set is EMPTY today, so no armed pilot may run. There is no CLI override, environment-variable override, manifest exemption, target allowlist, operator acknowledgement, hidden flag or downgrade from refusal to warning.

set.state: DECIDED (owner), replacing the rev 25 OPEN item. Phase 18 supports ONLY an exact browser binary and launch configuration that passes the COMPLETE W6-T SharedWorker conformance gate. The capability probe must execute in the SAME browser process, browser context configuration, executable, arguments, environment and security posture that the pilot run will use (the same-process rule). The currently pinned Chromium build is UNSUPPORTED for arming because SharedWorker is present. Firefox and WebKit must not be substituted, no older browser may be selected, and no undocumented feature flag may be used. No operational browser may be claimed to exist until one passes the complete gate; the SUPPORTED-BROWSER SET IS EMPTY TODAY. A safe refusal is an acceptable Phase 18 result: components that do not depend on arming may be implemented later in the approved PR sequence, but NO customer pilot may execute while the supported set is empty. If the probed browser process exits, crashes, relaunches, changes executable or arguments, or creates a differently configured context, the approval is INVALID and the complete probe runs again before any target access. No probe result may be transferred to another browser process or cached across launches.

ADDRESSED. One order is chosen and stated: unverified/malformed evidence precedes measured presence, evaluated across ALL required realms rather than stopping at the first matching realm. Rev 26 states which outcomes SPIKEW-06 actually exercised under the old first-match order and that the default build's reason under rev 26 would be shared_worker_block_unverified rather than the shared_worker_present that SPIKEW-06 printed. Both are exit-18 refusals; this is a reason-code change only.

ADDRESSED. The 'isolated world' claim is removed from rev 25 B.2, B.6 and FC3 and from the SPIKE-W6 findings text. Accurate statement: Playwright page.evaluate/frame.evaluate normally execute in the page's MAIN world. Probe integrity rests on a Falcon-authored local document evaluated BEFORE any external target access, on capturing the required native references before any mutable page code runs, on validating the exact browser process and launch configuration (the same-process rule of OWNER-24), and on failing closed on any inconsistency. F17 and F18 (realms created after the probe or after arming) need the same care and stay fail-closed until measured.
